\section[das Mittelalter]{das Mittelalter — the Middle Ages}

\label{lesson:GE-C320-mittelalter}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to conquer, then the German for the victory.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: das Mittelalter}
\textbf{das Mittelalter} — \textquotedblleft{}the Middle Ages\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Im Mittelalter war die Stadt sehr klein.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In the Middle Ages the town was very small.}
\end{quote}

No plural. \emph{Mittelalterlich} — medieval.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Mittelalter} joins \emph{mittel-} \textquotedblleft{}middle\textquotedblright{} and \emph{Alter} \textquotedblleft{}age\textquotedblright{}, from Old High German \emph{altar}, Proto-Germanic \emph{aldrą} \textquotedblleft{}life, age\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): the age in the middle.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{das Mittelalter}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{das Mittelalter}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{das Mittelalter}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for to conquer, then the German for the victory, then say \emph{das Mittelalter} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does das Mittelalter mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The Middle Ages\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[die Antike]{die Antike — antiquity, the ancient world}

\label{lesson:GE-C320-antike}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the victory, then the German for the Middle Ages.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: die Antike}
\textbf{die Antike} — \textquotedblleft{}antiquity, the ancient world\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Der Tempel ist aus der Antike.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The temple dates from antiquity.}
\end{quote}

No plural for the period. \emph{Antik} — antique.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Antike} is built on \emph{antik} \textquotedblleft{}ancient\textquotedblright{}, borrowed from French \emph{antique}, from Latin \emph{antīquus} \textquotedblleft{}old, former\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{die Antike}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for the victory, then the German for the Middle Ages, then say \emph{die Antike} again
\end{itemize}

\section[die Chronik]{die Chronik — the chronicle}

\label{lesson:GE-C320-chronik}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the Middle Ages, then the German for antiquity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: die Chronik}
\textbf{die Chronik} — \textquotedblleft{}the chronicle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
In der Chronik der Stadt steht das Jahr des Feuers.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The year of the fire is in the town chronicle.}
\end{quote}

Plural: \emph{die Chroniken}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Chronik} comes from Latin \emph{chronica}, from Greek \emph{khronikos} \textquotedblleft{}of or about time\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{khronos} \textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{die Chronik}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{die Chronik}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for the Middle Ages, then the German for antiquity, then say \emph{die Chronik} again

\section[der Vorfahr]{der Vorfahr — the ancestor}

\label{lesson:GE-C320-vorfahr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for antiquity, then the German for the chronicle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: der Vorfahr}
\textbf{der Vorfahr} — \textquotedblleft{}the ancestor\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Seine Vorfahren waren Bauern.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{His ancestors were farmers.}
\end{quote}

Weak noun, often in the plural: \emph{die Vorfahren}. Also \emph{der Vorfahre}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Vorfahr} joins \emph{vor} \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{} and the root of \emph{fahren} \textquotedblleft{}to travel, to go\textquotedblright{}, an inherited Germanic verb: one who went before. EtymDB lists no parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[der Untergang]{der Untergang — the downfall, the sinking}

\label{lesson:GE-C320-untergang}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the chronicle, then the German for the ancestor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: der Untergang}
\textbf{der Untergang} — \textquotedblleft{}the downfall, the sinking\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Der Untergang des Schiffes war eine Katastrophe.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The sinking of the ship was a disaster.}
\end{quote}

Plural: \emph{die Untergänge}. \emph{Der Sonnenuntergang} — sunset.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Untergang} is built on \emph{untergehen} \textquotedblleft{}to go down\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{unter} \textquotedblleft{}under\textquotedblright{} and \emph{Gang} \textquotedblleft{}a going\textquotedblright{}, from the root of \emph{gehen} \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright
